content.text: The text reviews historical treatment of dysentery, including diet, opium, astringents, ergotin, transfusion, and climate change. It then discusses typhlitis, perityphlitis, and paratyphlitis: causes include appendiceal obstruction, fecal concretions, foreign bodies, infection, and anatomical anomalies; symptoms include right iliac pain, fever, vomiting, constipation, tumors, perforation, and peritonitis. Intestinal ulcers may arise from dysentery, typhoid, tuberculosis, toxins, trauma, or peptic disease, causing pain, diarrhea, hemorrhage, and stenosis. The text also covers bowel hemorrhage, obstruction, intussusception, volvulus, strictures, cancer, rectal disease, hemorrhoids, fissures, abscesses, fistulas, syphilis, tuberculosis, and treatment ranging from diet and opium to irrigation, aspiration, colotomy, and laparotomy. Daniel journeyed to the garden; John moved to the garden.
